newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet fuel supported by purchase.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet fuel supported by purchase.

text.p: Jet fuel in Singapore continued to get support from a local trader with another 200,000 barrels traded at around $25.00 per barrel, traders said on Wednesday.

One cargo for May 1-5 lifting was done at $25.00 per barrel and the second cargo was done at $25.60, free-on-board basis, both from a European major. The buyer also took the same volumes from the major on Tuesday.
But traders said regional demand remained weak as few sale outlets were available and values would not be able to hold at current levels if not for the trader's continued purchases.
Gas oil also remained supported at around $27.00 per barrel, as the same Singapore trader bought 150,000 barrels from a French refiner at that level for May 11-15 lifting.
The French refiner has so far sold five cargoes to the Singapore trader.
Arbitrage cargoes continued to be offered. A Swiss trader offered a 300,000-barrel cargo on a cost-and-freight basis at $26.80, for May 8-12, off-port limits.
A South Korean refiner was also offering 30,000 tonnes of gas oil for end April lifting at 30 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, fob.
Traders said few discussions were heard about sales to Hong Kong and southern China.
Sri Lanka would decide Thursday on its mid-May diesel and jet fuel tender, a Colombo source said.
